result.reason: The passage is the Mishnah text about tevul yom and other impure persons' liquids (rishon status, av hatumah exception) that the prose of heading 5 'Tevul Yom Status' directly explains and discusses in detail.

Both items directly address the zav vs. corpse distinction — item 1 clarifies that 'minor/major' sources refer to creeping animal vs. zav, and item 2 gives the rationale for why rabbis decreed on zav but not corpse — exactly the content described in the 'Zav vs. Corpse Logic' prose.

All three items together constitute exactly the three-way dispute (Rabbanan, Rabbi Yehuda, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel) over 'damo' and the obligation to cover splattered blood and blood on the knife, which is precisely what the 'Damo Debate' prose describes in detail.

The passage is the Mishnah text itself listing what materials may and may not be used for kissuy hadam, which is precisely what the 'Granular vs. Thick' section's prose introduces and discusses — it is the source text for that section, not for the RSBG principle section which discusses the subsequent klal.

Both items discuss the definition of fine vs. thick sand via the potter's standard and the practical difference between the two formulations, which is precisely what the 'Potter's Standard' prose section discusses in detail.

All four items — the baraita deriving permissible covering materials, the inclusion/exclusion reasoning, and the klal u'prat challenge — are explicitly quoted and discussed in the prose under heading 0 ('Klal Tzarich l'Prat'), which walks through each of these Talmudic passages in sequence.
The passage is Rav Mari's statement about klal hatzarich liprat, which is precisely what the 'Rashi & Tosafot' section's prose discusses and analyzes in detail.

Both items concern Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda's teaching that only sprouting substances may be used and Rava's challenge to it — this is the derivation of the 'megadel tzma'chim' criterion, which is the subject of the 'Ribuy u'Miut Method' / klal u'prat prose, not the extreme desert/ship cases themselves.

The passage directly discusses the Gemara's question about the basis for using ashes and gold dust, and Rabbi Zeira's answer from the verse 'afrot zahav lo,' which is precisely what the 'Ashes & Gold Dust' section's prose discusses.
The passage is the Beit Shammai/Beit Hillel baraita about covering blood with earth vs. ashes, which is precisely what the 'Core Dispute' prose discusses in detail.
The passage directly discusses the added materials (coal dust, stibium, shavings, arsenic) which is exactly what the 'Added Materials' prose section addresses.

All three items belong to the continuous aggadic passage about Avraham's reward — items 1-2 are the challenge and response about kissuy hadam, and item 3 opens another Rava statement — but candidate 0 ('Avraham's Statement') covers items 1-2 while candidate 1 ('Why Not Kissuy') covers items 1-2's challenge-response, and since the prose of candidate 0 explicitly discusses Rava's statement about afar and eifer (items 1-2) while item 3 begins a new Rava statement, the current placement under candidate 0 is the best fit for all three items as a unified aggadic block.
